companies.name: Neuralink
companies.description: Fully implanted, wireless BCI with ultra-thin threads placed by a surgical robot; in human trials for controlling computers by thought.

companies.name: Synchron
companies.description: Stentrode, an endovascular BCI delivered through a blood vessel instead of open-brain surgery.

companies.name: Precision Neuroscience
companies.description: Layer 7, a thin-film electrode array that sits on the brain's surface without penetrating tissue; FDA-cleared for temporary use.

companies.name: Paradromics
companies.description: Connexus, a high-channel-count implanted BCI aimed at restoring speech for people with paralysis.

companies.name: Blackrock Neurotech
companies.description: Maker of the Utah Array, the most widely implanted BCI electrode in human research.

companies.name: Science Corp
companies.description: Neural engineering company behind PRIMA, a retinal implant that restores some vision, plus biohybrid brain interfaces.

companies.name: Motif Neurotech
companies.description: DOT, a tiny skull-mounted stimulator for treatment-resistant depression; a Rice University spinout.

companies.name: Axoft
companies.description: Ultra-soft implant materials that match brain tissue, for long-lasting neural interfaces.

companies.name: Echo Neurotechnologies
companies.description: Implanted BCI that decodes speech from brain activity; founded by UCSF neurosurgeon Eddie Chang.

companies.name: Starfish Neuroscience
companies.description: Small, low-power brain chips for neuromodulation and recording; co-founded by Gabe Newell.

companies.name: Phantom Neuro
companies.description: Minimally invasive implanted nerve interface for controlling prosthetic limbs.

companies.name: CorTec
companies.description: Brain Interchange, a closed-loop implant for recording and stimulating the brain; first US implant for stroke rehab in 2025.

companies.name: INBRAIN Neuroelectronics
companies.description: Graphene-based brain interfaces for Parkinson's and brain mapping; based in Barcelona.

companies.name: Diagnostic Biochips
companies.description: Microfabricated implantable neural probes for high-resolution brain recording in research.

companies.name: Ripple Neuro
companies.description: Neural recording and stimulation electronics used in implant research and clinical BCI studies.

companies.name: Intan Technologies
companies.description: Amplifier chips and recording systems used in electrophysiology labs worldwide.

companies.name: Merge Labs
companies.description: BCI that links to neurons with molecules and reads and writes with ultrasound instead of implanted electrodes; backed by OpenAI.

companies.name: Nudge
companies.description: Whole-brain interfaces for everyday life, using focused ultrasound to read and stimulate the brain without surgery.

companies.name: Bridge Neurotech
companies.description: Wearable ultrasound that images brain activity in real time without surgery; first study enrolling in Redwood City.

companies.name: Subsense
companies.description: Non-surgical, two-way BCI built on nanoparticles that are read and controlled by a wearable headset.

companies.name: Sabi
companies.description: Sabi Cap, a high-density EEG wearable plus a brain foundation model that turns imagined speech into text.

companies.name: Alljoined
companies.description: Collecting large EEG datasets and training models to make human thought legible to AI.

companies.name: Synaptrix Labs
companies.description: Non-invasive EEG-based BCI hardware and ML, from electrode arrays to embedded systems; based in NYC.

companies.name: Kernel
companies.description: Kernel Flow, a wearable fNIRS headset that measures brain activity for research and brain health.

companies.name: Neurable
companies.description: EEG sensors built into everyday headphones to track focus and fatigue.

companies.name: Cognixion
companies.description: Cognixion ONE, an EEG + augmented reality headset that helps people with ALS and similar conditions communicate.

companies.name: InteraXon
companies.description: Muse, the consumer EEG (and fNIRS) headband for meditation and sleep; based in Toronto.

companies.name: Emotiv
companies.description: Wireless EEG headsets and earbuds for research, wellness, and BCI software development.

companies.name: OpenBCI
companies.description: Open-source EEG/EMG hardware and software, including the Galea headset for XR research.

companies.name: Neurosity
companies.description: Crown, a developer-focused EEG headset with an SDK for building BCI apps.

companies.name: Arctop
companies.description: Software that decodes focus, cognitive load, and attention from EEG in everyday headphones, in real time.

companies.name: BrainCo
companies.description: EEG headbands and EMG-controlled prosthetic hands; a Harvard spinout based in Somerville and Hangzhou.

companies.name: NextSense
companies.description: EEG earbuds that adapt audio to your brain activity for better sleep; a Google X spinout.

companies.name: Elemind
companies.description: A headband that reads EEG and plays timed sound to help you fall asleep faster.

companies.name: Openwater
companies.description: Low-cost, open-source devices that image and stimulate the body and brain with light and ultrasound.

companies.name: Piramidal
companies.description: Foundation models for EEG that read brain signals at the level of clinical experts.

companies.name: NeuroPace
companies.description: RNS System, an implanted device that detects and stops seizures in drug-resistant epilepsy.

companies.name: Ceribell
companies.description: Rapid-setup EEG headband with AI seizure detection, used in emergency rooms and ICUs.

companies.name: Beacon Biosignals
companies.description: AI on EEG and sleep data for clinical trials and at-home brain monitoring.

companies.name: Cala Health
companies.description: Wrist-worn nerve stimulation therapy for essential tremor.

companies.name: ONWARD Medical
companies.description: Spinal cord stimulation systems (ARC-EX, ARC-IM) that help people with spinal cord injury regain movement.

companies.name: Neuronetics
companies.description: NeuroStar, a TMS (magnetic brain stimulation) therapy for depression.

companies.name: Medtronic
companies.description: The largest medical device company; its neuromodulation unit makes deep brain stimulation systems that sense brain signals.

companies.name: Boston Scientific
companies.description: Medical devices, including Vercise deep brain stimulation and spinal cord stimulators for chronic pain.

companies.name: Abbott
companies.description: Healthcare company whose neuromodulation unit makes deep brain and spinal cord stimulation systems.

companies.name: Metamorphic
companies.description: Foundation models trained on large-scale neural recordings, from the team behind MICrONS and Neuropixels.

companies.name: Convergent Research
companies.description: Runs nonprofit research groups, including E11 Bio (brain mapping) and Arbor Neuroscience (ultrasound brain imaging, formerly Forest Neurotech).

companies.name: Meta
companies.description: Reality Labs builds the EMG wristband neural interface for controlling AR glasses, plus brain-decoding research at FAIR.

companies.name: Google DeepMind
companies.description: AI research lab with neuroscience-inspired research teams.

companies.name: Allen Institute
companies.description: Nonprofit research institute that builds open brain atlases, cell types data, and large-scale neural recordings.

companies.name: HHMI Janelia
companies.description: HHMI's research campus focused on neural circuits, imaging, and tools like Neuropixels.

companies.name: Simons Foundation
companies.description: Funds and runs science research, including the Flatiron Institute's computational neuroscience center.

companies.name: Wu Tsai Neurosciences Institute
companies.description: Stanford's interdisciplinary neuroscience institute.

companies.name: Mila
companies.description: Quebec AI institute in Montreal, with some neuro-AI research groups.

companies.name: Vector Institute
companies.description: Toronto AI research institute, including health and neuro applications.

companies.name: University Health Network
companies.description: Toronto hospital network; home of the Krembil Brain Institute.

companies.name: Djavad Mowafaghian Centre for Brain Health
companies.description: UBC's brain health research centre in Vancouver.
